The asserted consequence is noetherianity. For an affine open Spec B⊂X, choose a finitely generated integral k-subalgebra A⊂K with Frac(A)=K and put S=A∖{0}. The canonical map b⊗(a/s)↦(b⊗a)/(1⊗s) gives the isomorphism B⊗_k K ≅ S^{-1}(B⊗_k A). The ring B⊗_k A is finitely generated over the noetherian ring B, hence noetherian, and its localization is noetherian. A finite affine cover of X gives a finite such cover of X_K, proving that X_K is noetherian. The printed finite-type-over-the-base conclusion fails in the exact identity-base-change example X=Spec k(u), K=k: X is noetherian and K/k is finitely generated, but X_K=X is not of finite type over k, since Zariski’s lemma would force the field k(u), if finitely generated as a k-algebra, to be finite algebraic over k.
